_readme: Configuration for editor.html. Everything here is PUBLIC by design and none
of it is a secret: a Client ID identifies the app, it does not authorise
anything. The secret half of the pair lives in the token exchange's
environment and never enters this repo.
clientId   the OAuth app. Public by construction, and it authorises nothing.
It does NOT keep a code out of anyone's hands: registration
controls where GitHub delivers a code, so a copy of this id on
another page receives nothing — but anyone may take the id to
GitHub, authorise the app against their own account, and read a
valid code out of their own address bar. What makes such a code
worthless is the owner check in worker/index.js, which refuses to
return a token for anyone but OWNER. That check is the security
boundary of this project; nothing here is.
on someone else's page receives nothing.
owner/repo the one repository the editor may write to.
branch     the branch notes are committed to. Must be the DEFAULT branch,
or the commits will not appear on the contributions calendar.
path       the store inside that repository.
scope      public_repo is enough for a public repository and is the least
privilege that works. If siddheshthapa is private this must be
repo, which is a wider grant - prefer keeping the repo public.
exchange   URL of the tiny function that swaps an OAuth code for a token,
because that swap needs the client secret and a browser cannot
hold one. Left empty until it is deployed; while it is empty the
editor says so plainly instead of failing at the last step.
AUTHORISATION IS NOT DECIDED HERE. The editor asks GitHub who you are and
whether you can push to this repository, and believes the answer. Editing
any value in this file changes which repository is addressed, never who is
allowed to write to it.
